S1.why: Short label like a price tag; 'בחינם' is the everyday word, and the digit before it makes the line read right-to-left.

S2.why: A plain question in the plural address the vocabulary uses; invites, names no limit, sells nothing.

S3.s: כל %lld הקאטלינגים החינמיים שלכם בשימוש. הם יישארו בחינם ויעבדו כמו תמיד.
S3.back: all 5 the-cutlings the-free yours in-use. they will-stay for-free and-will-work like always.
S3.why: 'קאטלינגים' is the vocabulary's item word in plural; second sentence is the reassurance, in future tense because it promises.

S4.why: Impersonal 'אפשר' is how Israeli apps state an allowance; no 'you can' address needed.

S5.why: 'X מתוך Y' is the natural Hebrew count; number order matches, so plain %lld; the noun agrees with the total, so it works for 1 used too.

S6.why: Noun phrase as a bold row line; maqaf joins the prefix ל to the number.

S7.s: אפשר לשמור עד %@ טקסטים ו־%lld תמונות.
S7.back: possible to-save up-to 5,000 texts and-500 images.
S7.why: 'טקסט' and 'תמונות' are the vocabulary's kind words; 'טקסטים' is the normal spoken plural.

S8.why: Hebrew repeats the prefix on each item and joins the last with ו; starting with Hebrew keeps the line right-to-left so the three names stay in order.

S9.s: רכישה אחת מספיקה לכל המכשירים שמחוברים לחשבון Apple שלכם.
S9.back: purchase one suffices for-all the-devices that-connected to-account Apple yours.
S9.why: 'מחוברים לחשבון Apple שלכם' is the vocabulary's own phrasing; 'רכישה' is Apple's Hebrew word for a purchase.

S10.why: Impersonal present plural, the way Israelis say how a thing works; nothing recurring is implied.

S11.s: בלי מנוי, בלי פרסומות ובלי הרשמה.
S11.back: without subscription, without ads and-without sign-up.
S11.why: The repeated 'בלי' with ו on the last is the native list of absences; 'הרשמה' is what Israeli apps call signing up.

S12.why: The wording Hebrew iOS apps use for Restore Purchases.

S13.why: 'מתבצע' plus noun is the standard Hebrew progress line; single ellipsis character.

S14.why: A noun on the button as Hebrew iOS buttons do; 'שדרוג' (upgrade) is what Israeli apps call a paid unlock, and 'חד־פעמי' carries 'pay once'.

S15.why: S14 without the price, so the button keeps its words when the price arrives.

S16.why: The usual polite put-off in Hebrew; says not now, not no.

S17.why: Hebrew iOS labels actions with the verbal noun; 'סגירה' is its Close.

S18.why: Short, warm and a little proud; 'הכול' covers all the room without counting it.

S19.s: תודה על הרכישה. היא עוזרת לקאטלינג ולאדם היחיד שבונה אותו.
S19.back: thanks for the-purchase. it helps to-Cutling and-to-the-person the-only who-builds it.
S19.why: Cutling without the article is the app's name; 'האדם היחיד שבונה אותו' keeps the one maker personal, not a company.

S20.s: ברוכים השבים. הרכישה הקודמת שלכם חזרה.
S20.back: blessed the-returners. the-purchase the-previous yours returned.
S20.why: 'ברוכים השבים' is the idiomatic welcome back; 'חזרה' says it is back without system words.

S21.why: Same count shape as S5, for speech; the noun follows the total, so 0, 1 or 3 used all read correctly.

S22.s: יש עכשיו מקום ל־%2$@ קאטלינגים, ומתוכם %1$lld בשימוש
S22.back: there-is now room for-5,000 cutlings, and-of-them 5 in-use
S22.why: Hebrew puts a bare count after 'ומתוכם', so 1, 2, 5 and 21 all read correctly with no plural form; the room comes first, hence positional placeholders.

S23.s: הגרסה המלאה פעילה. יש מקום ל־%@ קאטלינגים.
S23.back: the-version the-full active. there-is room for-5,000 cutlings.
S23.why: 'הגרסה המלאה' names the bought state everywhere, so the app's name and the item word, which are spelled the same, never meet in one line.

S24.why: Calm statement of what happened; no subject to blame.

S25.s: אין כרגע חיבור ל־App Store. נסו שוב בעוד כמה רגעים.
S25.back: there-isn't currently connection to-App-Store. try(pl) again in a-few moments.
S25.why: Opens in Hebrew so the alert lays out right-to-left; 'נסו' is the vocabulary's plural address.

S26.s: לא התקבל אישור מ־App Store לרכישה הזו.
S26.back: not received confirmation from-App-Store for-the-purchase this.
S26.why: Passive 'לא התקבל' keeps the line calm and puts the store second, so the sentence opens in Hebrew.

S27.s: לא נמצאה רכישה קודמת של קאטלינג בחשבון Apple שמחובר למכשיר הזה.
S27.back: not found purchase previous of Cutling in-account Apple that-connected to-the-device this.
S27.why: 'שמחובר' follows the vocabulary's account phrasing; Cutling without article is the app.

S28.s: בגרסה החינמית יש מקום ל־%lld קאטלינגים. אחרי שדרוג חד־פעמי אפשר לשמור כמה שרוצים.
S28.back: in-the-version the-free there-is room for-5 cutlings. after upgrade one-time possible to-save as-many-as wanted.
S28.why: 'הגרסה החינמית' pairs with 'הגרסה המלאה'; 'שדרוג חד־פעמי' is the button's own words.

S29.why: Compact count under the list title, which already says קאטלינג, so the noun is left out.

K1.why: One capsule line: 'החינמיים' stands for the items since space is short; 'הקישו' is the Hebrew iOS verb for tap.

M1.why: Verbal noun first, as Hebrew Mac window and menu titles are written.

M2.why: Same command as M1, with the ellipsis because it opens a window.

M3.why: Row label in the item word's plural.

M4.why: 'מתוך' is how Hebrew reads a pair; a slash would read as a date or fraction.

M5.why: Status in the same words VoiceOver announces at the unlock.

M6.s: רכישה אחת לגרסה המלאה ב־iPhone, ב־iPad וב־Mac.
M6.back: purchase one for-the-version the-full on-iPhone, on-iPad and-on-Mac.
M6.why: Same three-device list as S8; opens in Hebrew.

M7.s: הגרסה המלאה פעילה ב־iPhone, ב־iPad וב־Mac עם חשבון Apple הזה.
M7.back: the-version the-full active on-iPhone, on-iPad and-on-Mac with account Apple this.
M7.why: Reuses M5's status and S8's list.

M8.s: קניתם את קאטלינג לפני שהפך לחינמי, ולכן הגרסה המלאה נשארת שלכם. תודה שהייתם כאן מההתחלה.
M8.back: bought(pl) ACC Cutling before that-became free, and-so the-version the-full stays yours. thanks that-you-were here from-the-start.
M8.why: Past plural address; the thanks is for coming early, which is what sets these buyers apart.
